newsitem.title: FRANCE: Opposition leader finds common ground with Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Opposition leader finds common ground with Mobutu.

text.p: Zairean radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi met ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko in southern France on Thursday and said they agreed on the need for national reconciliation.

"What is happening today is that the leaders of two tendencies are merging into one. It's a question of responsibility," he said, referring to the Rwandan-backed rebellion now controlling large areas of eastern Zaire.
"The people needed to have confidence...What was needed was the unity of the country's politicians," said Tshisekedi, who last week said he was prepared to form a government to resolve the crisis.
Tshisekedi had flown to Nice from Paris earlier in the day to meet Mobutu, who is convalescing in a private mansion on the Riviera after cancer surgery in August.

Speaking to reporters, Tshisekedi denied he sought to replace the president but said: "If the people do not want me as prime minister, so be it because my ambition is to be at the service of the people."

Tshisekedi, principal figure in the opposition to Mobutu, still claims to be Zaire's prime minister, a post he held in 1992. Mobutu pushed him aside the following year and the two last met officially in December 1992.
Current Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo meanwhile said in Kinshasa that Mobutu would be back home before the end of the month.
"He himself has said that he will have a medical checkup on the 25th of November, and will return home three days later," said Kengo who last week met Mobutu in southern France.

Mobutu, in power in Zaire for three decades, said in an interview with CNN that he had been stabbed in the back during his absence by "devils" invading the east of Zaire. "After my convalescence, I'll return to Zaire as president," he said.
Mobutu arrived in France from Switzerland on November 4 planning to stay for several weeks and has held a string of consultations on the crisis at his villa at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin near Nice.
Since arriving in France, Mobutu has also met U.N. envoy Raymond Chretien, Congo President Pascal Lissouba and Gabonese President Omar Bongo.
